text: Large Language Models, or LLMs, are computer programs trained on vast amounts of text from books, articles, and websites. They learn patterns in language, which lets them predict the next word in a sequence. This is why they can write essays, answer questions, or even create code. To use them well, people practice prompt engineering—writing clear, specific instructions to get better results. However, LLMs have limits. They can make up facts or sound confident when wrong, and they don’t truly understand meaning. They also can’t access real-time information unless connected to the internet. So, while powerful, they are tools to assist, not replace, human judgment.
